arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Roberts argued the Act contains automatic exclusions for pretrial proceedings.
Justice Sotomayor questioned the benefit to defendants with violated rights.
Justice Alito asked if deciding on subsection F makes subsection D dictum.
Justice Ginsburg asked if Congress expected judges to set dates after motions.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the Speedy Trial Act. It asks if certain pretrial motions stop the clock. The government argues these motions pause the deadline. The defendant argues the deadline continues running.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government wants the Court to exclude pretrial motion time from the deadline.
The defendant wants the Court to include that time in the deadline calculation.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues the Act automatically excludes time for important pretrial proceedings.
The defendant argues the statutory text does not support excluding this specific time.

paragraphs: This case defines how courts calculate trial deadlines. It affects every criminal defendant facing pretrial motions. It clarifies the scope of the Speedy Trial Act. It shapes how judges manage court calendars.
